To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

consumers' perceptions regarding the trust and expertise of a firm providing automated financial advice through a computer algorithm are important drivers of the consumer acceptance of this advice and that these constructs are strongly influenced by two key characteristics of the firm, namely its profit orientation and the role it plays in the financial sales channel.

the acceptance of automated financial advice depends on consumer perceptions of trust and expertness of the provider of the advice and that these perceptions are influenced by the profit orientation and the role in the sales chain of the provider.
consumers' perceptions about a firm's trust and expertise, as well as their satisfaction with the automated tool, are key drivers of the acceptance of automated pension advice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether consumers accept automated financial advice.
how consumers evaluate and accept automated financial advice.
the acceptance of computer generated advice in a real world setting and the role of firm characteristics on this acceptance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the acceptance of automated financial advice is a complex process and the acceptance of automated advice by a consumer is influenced by a number of firm characteristics.
consumers are more likely to accept advice provided by computer algorithms if they perceive the advice provider as trustworthy and expert.
the acceptance of financial robo advice is a complex phenomenon and is driven by multiple factors that are not necessarily independent from each other.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the acceptance of automated financial advice is influenced by the trust and expertise consumers perceive the firm providing the service to possess and that these constructs are clearly influenced by firm characteristics.

consumers' perceptions about firms' motives and their role in the sales process are important drivers of their trust and expertise of firms and that these perceptions influence their acceptance of advice from automated online tools.

the role of trust and expertise is a key factor for the acceptance of robo advice and that this acceptance is influenced by the firm characteristics of profit orientation and role of the sales channel.
The main takeaway from our work is that

firms that want to be successful in providing financial advice through automated online tools need to be aware of the importance of their firm characteristics and the impact they have on consumer perceptions of trust and expertness.
the acceptance of automated financial advice is a function of the trust and expertise perceptions of the firm providing such advice.
the acceptance of automated financial advice is not just about the algorithm but also about the trust and expertise that individuals attribute to the firm behind it.
